title: The Two Sneaky Numbers of Digitville
statement: The array `nums` was meant to hold every integer from `0` to `n - 1` exactly once. Instead, two different integers each turn up one extra time, so `nums` has `n + 2` elements: every value from `0` to `n - 1` occurs once, except those two, which occur twice. Return the two repeated values as an array of length 2, in any order.
constraints: Exactly two values repeat, each appearing twice; every other value from 0 to n - 1 appears once
notes:
## Intuition

Each value belongs in `nums` once, so a sneaky value is exactly one that shows up when it has already been seen. Counting every value with a fresh scan would cost O(n²); remembering the values met so far in a set finds both repeats in a single pass.

## Approach

1. Start with an empty set `seen` and an empty list `sneaky`.
2. Walk through `nums`. If `num` is already in `seen`, this is its second appearance, so add it to `sneaky`.
3. Otherwise record `num` in `seen`.
4. After the scan `sneaky` holds the two repeated values; return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [0, 1, 1, 0]`.

- `0` is new: `seen = {0}`.
- `1` is new: `seen = {0, 1}`.
- `1` is already in `seen`: `sneaky = [1]`.
- `0` is already in `seen`: `sneaky = [1, 0]`.

The answer `[1, 0]` holds the same values as `[0, 1]`, and any order is accepted.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one set lookup per element.
- Space: O(n) for `seen`.

## Pitfalls

- There are two sneaky values: returning at the first repeat finds only one of them.
- Keeping `seen` as an array and searching it with `includes` makes every lookup O(n) and the whole scan O(n²).
- For O(1) extra space, the sum alone is not enough: with sneaky values `x` and `y`, it exceeds the sum of `0..n-1` by `x + y`, which cannot separate them. The sum of squares exceeds its counterpart by `x² + y²`, and the two equations together determine both values.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | values met so far |
| `sneaky` | values met a second time |
| `num` | the current element of `nums` |

narration.2: seen remembers every value met so far.
narration.3: sneaky collects the values that appear a second time.
narration.4: Look at each element once, from left to right.
narration.5: Has this value been met before?
narration.6: Yes: this is its extra copy, so it is one of the two sneaky numbers.
narration.8: No: remember it so a later copy is recognised.
narration.11: Both repeats were found during the scan; return them in the order they were caught.
